sections.heading: Rahul and Arjun: the students from India who want to include their partners on their Temporary Graduate visas
sections.text:
Arjun is about to finish his Bachelor of Economics and wants to apply for a Temporary Graduate visa. Last year, he got married, but his wife was not included on his Student visa and remained in India.

Now that he is planning to apply for a Temporary Graduate visa, Arjun wants to include his wife as a family member in his visa application.

Rahul is also finishing his Bachelor of Economics and plans to apply for a Temporary Graduate visa as well. Unlike Arjun, Rahul’s wife was already included on his Student visa.

From 13 November 2026, new rules apply to family members who can be included in Temporary Graduate visa applications.

sections.heading: Rahul and Arjun: the students from India who want to include their partners on their Temporary Graduate visas > What do the new rules mean for Arjun and Rahul?
sections.text:
Arjun cannot include his wife because she was not included on his previous Student visa and he doesn’t meet any other eligibility criteria for including family.

Rahul, however, can include his wife in his visa application because she was already included on his previous Student visa. Rahul must be in Australia when he applies, and his wife can be inside or outside Australia when she applies. They must apply at the same time. Rahul cannot add her later as a subsequent entrant.

sections.heading: Lina is from an ASEAN member country and has a husband at home. He was not on her student visa.
sections.text:
Lina is from an ASEAN member country and is married. While Lina was studying a Bachelor of Education in Australia, her husband stayed in their home country.

Now that Lina has her teaching degree, she plans to apply for a Temporary Graduate visa and include her husband in her application.

From 13 November 2026, new rules apply to family members who can be included in Temporary Graduate visa applications.

sections.heading: Lina is from an ASEAN member country and has a husband at home. He was not on her student visa. > What do the new rules mean for Lina?
sections.text:
Lina can include her husband in her visa application because, as a passport holder of an ASEAN member country, she meets one of the exemption criteria. This means she can include her husband even though he was not included on her previous Student visa.

Lina must be in Australia when she applies for her visa. Her husband can be in or outside Australia when she applies, but they must apply at the same time. Lina cannot add him later as a subsequent entrant.

sections.heading: Cate who gave birth to her child in her home country, after her first Temporary Graduate visa was granted
sections.text:
Cate and her husband are from North America and are currently working in Western Australia on their first Temporary Graduate visa. Her husband is the primary applicant, and Cate is included as his dependant. One year after arriving in Australia, she became pregnant but decided to return to her home country to give birth so she could be closer to her parents.

Her Temporary Graduate visa is expiring soon, and her and her husband will be applying for their second Temporary Graduate visa.

She would like to add her baby to her Temporary Graduate visa.

From 13 November 2026, new rules apply to family members who can be included in Temporary Graduate visa applications.

sections.heading: Cate who gave birth to her child in her home country, after her first Temporary Graduate visa was granted > What do the new rules mean for Cate?
sections.text:
Under the new rules, family members (including newborn children) cannot apply to join a Temporary Graduate visa holder after the visa is granted.

Under the eligibility criteria, newborn children born after the primary applicant was granted their most recent Student visa or Temporary Graduate visa can be included on a new Temporary Graduate visa.

This means that Cate ‘s newborn child can be included on her new second Temporary Graduate visa application, even though her baby was not included on her previous visa application. Her newborn child cannot be added to her current Temporary Graduate visa.

Cate must be in Australia when she applies for the visa to add her baby. Her baby can be in or outside Australia when she applies.
